purpose: Tests order-dependence of E-null suffix pairs. Cross-role pairs (ASSERT x MISLEADING) test genuine monoid noncommutativity. Same-role pairs control for recency/attention-decay confound. The decisive criterion: cross-role TV(AB,BA) must EXCEED same-role TV(A1A2,A2A1). Surfaces should be prevalidated representatives from Gate 1b.
_NOTE: Surfaces below are PLACEHOLDERS. Must be replaced with Gate 1b prevalidated representatives (within-class TV < eps_eq, between-class TV > eps_sep). Token-length matching is desirable.

composition_pairs._label: cross-role: ASSERT_VAR x MISLEADING (the main test)
same-role control: ASSERT_VAR x ASSERT_VAR (recency null)
same-role control: MISLEADING x MISLEADING (recency null)

predictions.H_recency_only: Same-role TV(A1A2,A2A1) is comparable to cross-role TV(AB,BA). Order effects are from recency/position, not content. No native monoid structure.
predictions.H_content_noncommutative: Cross-role TV(AB,BA) >> same-role TV(A1A2,A2A1). Order effect is content-dependent. Genuine non-scalar monoid action.
predictions.decisive_criterion: Cross-role median TV exceeds same-role max TV AND exceeds eps_eq. Must hold across multiple prevalidated representative pairs to establish class-level (not string-level) noncommutativity.

estimated_calls: 3 pairs x 5 conditions x 24 contexts = 360 calls, ~7.5 min CPU
